title: Stroke Studio, Custom Dashes & Vector Pressure Curves
subtitle: 4 Dash/Gap Sequences, Pressure Graph Tapering & Presets

learningObjectives: Master the advanced controls of the Stroke Studio: Width, Alignment (Center, Inside, Outside), Caps, and Joins.
Design complex rhythmic dashed lines using the 4 dash/gap pattern input matrix.
Sculpt variable-width calligraphy and hair strands using the interactive Stroke Pressure Graph.
Save, manage, and recall custom stroke pressure presets across vector illustration projects.
standardSections.foundationalKnowledge: In basic graphic design, vector strokes have a uniform, rigid thickness from start to finish. In high-end digital illustration and calligraphy, organic strokes require dynamic weight variation: thin delicate hairlines that swell into thick bold curves and taper gracefully into razor-sharp points. Rather than requiring you to outline paths and manually nudge hundreds of Bezier nodes, Affinity Designer incorporates a real-time 'Pressure Studio' into every vector stroke. An interactive pressure curve graph maps stroke width dynamically along the path length, transforming a single mathematical curve into expressive, responsive brushwork.

technicalEvidence.source: Affinity Designer 3.3.3 Stroke Studio & Pressure Graph Specification

shortcut.mac: View > Studio > Stroke (or Context Bar stroke swatch)

stepByStepInstructions.title: Draw a Freehand or Pen Path
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Using the Pen Tool (P) or Vector Brush Tool, draw an elegant S-shaped curve on your artboard.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Configure Stroke Weight in the Stroke Studio
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Open the Stroke Studio (View > Studio > Stroke). Set the width to 32 pt so that pressure variations are clearly visible. Set Cap to 'Round Cap'.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Open the Pressure Graph
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: At the bottom of the Stroke Studio, click the 'Pressure' button. A popup graph appears with a horizontal line across the top (representing 100% stroke thickness along the path).

stepByStepInstructions.title: Sculpt a Calligraphic Taper Profile
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Drag the leftmost node of the graph down to 0% (path start is needle sharp). Click the middle of the graph line to add a center control node and pull it to 100% (thick belly). Drag the rightmost node down to 0% (path end is needle sharp). Observe your path instantly transform into an organic hand-lettered brush stroke!

stepByStepInstructions.title: Create a Custom Rhythmic Dash Pattern
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Draw a circle. In the Stroke Studio, switch Style to 'Dashed Line'. In the 4 dash boxes, enter: Dash 1: `6`, Gap 1: `2`, Dash 2: `2`, Gap 2: `2`. Notice a refined technical blueprint dash rhythm appear immediately around the circle.

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Stroke Pressure button is disabled (grayed out)
commonPitfalls.cause: The active stroke style is set to 'Dashed Line' or 'No Stroke'.
commonPitfalls.solution: Pressure curves only apply to continuous solid line styles. Set Style to 'Solid Line' in the Stroke Studio.

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Strokes ballooning when artwork is scaled down
commonPitfalls.cause: The 'Scale with object' checkbox is unchecked in the Stroke Studio.
commonPitfalls.solution: Always check 'Scale with object' so that stroke widths and pressure profiles scale proportionally with your illustration.

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Tapered stroke looking pixelated on canvas
commonPitfalls.cause: Viewing in Pixel Preview mode at a low zoom level.
commonPitfalls.solution: Switch to Vector View Mode (View > View Mode > Vector) to preview infinite mathematical Bezier curves.

knowledgeCheck.question: What is the primary architectural function of the 'Pressure' graph in the Affinity Designer Stroke Studio?
options: It measures how hard you press your keyboard keys.
It dynamically maps the thickness of a vector stroke along its length, allowing you to sculpt calligraphic tapers without outlining paths.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The Pressure graph allows artists to modulate the stroke width multiplier (0% to 100%) from the start node to the end node along any vector curve.

knowledgeCheck.question: How many independent Dash and Gap parameter pairs does Affinity Designer support in its custom dashed line engine?
options: Up to 4 pairs (Dash 1/Gap 1, Dash 2/Gap 2, Dash 3/Gap 3, Dash 4/Gap 4).
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Affinity Designer provides 4 consecutive pairs of Dash and Gap inputs, enabling intricate rhythmic dash sequences (such as Morse code or complex technical drafting lines).

knowledgeCheck.question: Why is the 'Scale with object' checkbox crucial when working with detailed vector strokes?
options: It forces the stroke to convert into an artboard.
It ensures the stroke width shrinks and enlarges proportionally when the shape is resized, preventing line weights from overwhelming miniaturized graphics.
It changes the stroke color to black.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Without 'Scale with object', a 20pt stroke remains 20pt even if you scale an icon down to 16x16 px, turning the artwork into a solid blob.

summaryPoints: The Stroke Studio provides comprehensive control over weight, caps, joins, and alignments.
The Pressure graph transforms uniform vector strokes into expressive, tapered brushwork.
Custom dash engines accept up to 4 dash/gap sequence pairs.
Always enable 'Scale with object' to guarantee scalable vector portability.

slides.title: Stroke Studio, Custom Dashes & Vector Pressure Curves
slides.subtitle: Breathing Organic Vitality into Precision Vector Linework
slides.contentMarkdown:
Welcome to **Lesson D04-02**.

Uniform strokes look mechanical. True illustration—from manga inking to luxury calligraphy—demands **variable-width strokes**.

In this lesson, you will master the **Stroke Studio Pressure Graph**, sculpt custom calligraphic tapers on single Bezier paths, and build complex **4-stage rhythmic dash patterns**.

actionBox.label: Illustration Breakthrough
actionBox.text: Never manually trace two sides of a tapered hair strand again! Draw a single line and sculpt it with Pressure.

slides.title: The Mechanics of the Pressure Graph
slides.subtitle: Mapping Width Multipliers Along a Bezier Curve
slides.contentMarkdown:
At the bottom of the Stroke Studio (`View > Studio > Stroke`), the **Pressure graph** modulates path thickness:

- **X-Axis:** Represents the chronological progression of the path from `0%` (Start Node) to `100%` (End Node).
- **Y-Axis:** Represents the stroke thickness multiplier from `0%` (razor-sharp hairline) to `100%` (maximum stroke width).
- **Control Nodes:** Click anywhere on the curve to add inflection points; drag nodes up or down to swell or pinch the stroke.

visual.content:
[100% Width] ────● (Thick Swell) ────
                 /                    \
  [0% Width]   ● (Sharp Taper)         ● (Sharp Taper)
               Start ═════════════════ End

slides.title: Stroke Alignment & Caps Refresher
slides.subtitle: Center, Inside & Outside Alignments
slides.contentMarkdown:
The Stroke Studio provides 3 essential alignment modes for closed shapes:

1. **Center Align:** The stroke straddles the path 50% inside, 50% outside (standard for illustration).
2. **Inner Align:** The entire stroke is clamped *inside* the vector boundary. Essential for UI buttons to prevent 1px boundary bleeding.
3. **Outer Align:** The entire stroke sits *outside* the boundary, preserving interior negative space.

actionBox.label: Golden Checkbox
actionBox.text: Always enable 'Scale with object' in the Stroke panel so strokes scale proportionally when graphics resize.

slides.title: Step-by-Step: Sculpting a Calligraphy Stroke
slides.subtitle: Executing the Pressure Taper Workflow
slides.contentMarkdown:
Follow these steps to turn a simple line into a calligraphic stroke:

1. **Step 1:** Select the Pen Tool (`P`) and draw a smooth curved flourish.
2. **Step 2:** In the Stroke Studio, set Width to `28 pt` and select **Round Cap**.
3. **Step 3:** Click the **'Pressure'** button at the bottom of the panel.
4. **Step 4:** Drag the left point down to `0%`. Drag the right point down to `0%`.
5. **Step 5:** Click the center of the graph line to add a node and drag it to `100%`.
6. **Step 6:** Click **'Save Profile'** to store this taper preset for future one-click use!

visual.content: Uniform 28pt Line (Mechanical) ===[ Pressure Graph ]===> Calligraphic Ribbon (Organic)

slides.title: Architectural Dashes: The 4-Pair Sequence
slides.subtitle: Creating Morse Code and Blueprint Patterns
slides.contentMarkdown:
Affinity Designer's dashed line engine is far more advanced than basic on/off toggles:

- It accepts **4 consecutive pairs** of Dash and Gap inputs.
- **Example 1 (Technical Blueprint):** `Dash 1: 8 | Gap 1: 2 | Dash 2: 2 | Gap 2: 2` (Long dash followed by dot).
- **Example 2 (Security Ticket):** `Dash 1: 12 | Gap 1: 3 | Dash 2: 4 | Gap 2: 3 | Dash 3: 4 | Gap 3: 3`.
- **Phase Offset:** Shift the phase slider to align corner dashes neatly without clipping.

visual.content:
| Pattern Name | Dash 1 / Gap 1 | Dash 2 / Gap 2 | Visual Rhythm |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | 3 / 3 | - | ──  ──  ──  ── |
| Long-Short | 8 / 2 | 2 / 2 | ──── ─ ──── ─ |
| Stitched Seam | 4 / 2 | 4 / 2 | ── ── ── ── |

slides.title: Tablet Stylus Velocity & Pressure
slides.subtitle: Live Drawing with Wacom & Apple Pencil
slides.contentMarkdown:
If you use a drawing tablet (Wacom, iPad Sidecar, Huion):

1. Select the **Vector Brush Tool (`B`)**.
2. On the Context Toolbar, change Controller from 'None' to **'Pressure'** or **'Velocity'**.
3. Affinity Designer samples your hardware stylus pressure levels in real time at 120Hz, automatically recording custom pressure graphs onto every vector curve as you draw!

actionBox.label: Hardware Integration
actionBox.text: Every tablet stroke creates an editable vector path with an embedded Pressure curve.

slides.title: Stroke Studio Pitfalls & Troubleshooting
slides.subtitle: Avoid Common Vector Glitches
slides.contentMarkdown:
### 1. Pressure Button is Grayed Out
- **The Cause:** The stroke is set to 'Dashed Line' or has a texture brush nozzle applied.
- **The Fix:** Switch the stroke style back to **Solid Line**.

### 2. The Ballooning Stroke Trap
- **The Issue:** You shrink an icon from 500px down to 50px, and the 20pt stroke fills the entire icon with black.
- **The Fix:** Enable **'Scale with object'** in the Stroke Studio before resizing.

### 3. Asymmetrical Pressure on Symmetrical Shapes
- **The Fix:** Reset the Pressure curve by clicking the 'Reset' button inside the Pressure popup dialog.

visual.content: Scale With Object: Mandatory | Solid Style for Pressure | Reset Button Restores Flat Line

slides.title: Independent Challenge: Dynamic Manga Action Burst
slides.subtitle: Put Vector Pressure & Dashes into Practice
slides.contentMarkdown:
### Your Mission:
Construct a high-intensity manga action speed burst around a central crest:

1. Draw 8 radiating curved speed lines using the Pen Tool (`P`).
2. Configure a custom **Pressure profile**: `0%` start, rising sharply to `100%` width, and tapering back to `0%`.
3. Save the profile preset as **'Action Taper'** and apply it across all 8 lines.
4. Draw an outer circular border frame and apply a custom **4-pair dash pattern** (`8-2-2-2-2-2`).

### Acceptance Criteria:
- Speed lines feature razor-sharp tapered ends sculpted via Pressure.
- At least 1 pressure preset saved.
- Frame features 4-pair rhythmic dashes.
